text: {"question":"How do the authors show that the reduction of the Hubble tension in the dilaton and tachyon k‑essence models is not an artifact of a particular data set, and what specific evidence from the conclusion supports this claim?","reference_answer":"They argue that the parameter shifts induced by the k‑essence dynamics are stable across all the late‑Universe probes considered, indicating that the models’ ability to lower the inferred Hubble constant is intrinsic rather than dataset‑dependent. The conclusion notes that the model parameters remain unchanged when different combinations of supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and BAO data are used, and that the Planck H₀ prediction is shifted while the baryon density stays largely the same, reinforcing the robustness of the tension alleviation.","passage_1_contribution":"The abstract states that both k‑essence models provide substantial tension alleviation that is robust against the inclusion of independent late‑Universe datasets, regardless of whether the observations are supernovae alone or combined with cosmic chronometers and BAO.","passage_2_contribution":"The conclusion emphasizes that the inferred cosmological‑parameter shifts are stable and intrinsic to the k‑essence dynamics, not dependent on any particular observational probe, and that the model parameters are not dataset‑dependent while the Planck H₀ prediction is shifted and the baryon density is largely preserved.","joint_reason":"The abstract claims robustness of tension alleviation across datasets; the conclusion provides the specific evidence—stable parameter shifts and dataset‑independence—supporting that claim.","same_quantity":false}
